newsitem.title: USA: Mitchell Energy rating could be raised.
newsitem.headline: Mitchell Energy rating could be raised.

text.p: Duff & Phelps Credit Rating Co said Tuesday it put Mitchell Energy & Development Corp's triple-B-minus senior note rating on its rating watch list for a potential upgrade.
The move was spurred by Mitchell's announcement that it intends to sell its primary real estate holding, The Woodlands, the credit rating agency said. The rating affects about $600 million of debt.
"The sale of The Woodlands properties for $543 million represents a significant change in business mix for the company," Duff & Phelps said in a statement.
"Real estate operations accounted for 17.5 percent of adjusted operating income in fiscal 1997 and roughly 39 percent of assets at the January 31, 1997 fiscal year-end.

"Although Mitchell will still retain approximately $30 million in other real estate assets that it intends to divest, the company's focus will now be entirely on its higher-return energy businesses," the rating agency said.
"The sale is expected to provide Mitchell with approximately $465 million in after-tax proceeds.

"The company has indicated that a number of alternatives are being reviewed for using the proceeds, including increased spending on exploration and production (E&P), acquisitions, share repurchases, debt reduction and/or a special dividend.

"New investment in and expansion of the E&P and natural gas gathering and processing businesses or debt reduction would likely benefit the company. Significant share repurchases or a large special dividend would leave the company's credit profile relatively stable," Duff & Phelps said.
